case_name: Sushil Kumar Shukla vs State Of U.P. & Others
facts_of_case: Petitioner, a practicing lawyer, applied for grant of firearm licence but it was rejected by the District Magistrate, Allahabad. Petitioner filed writ petition No.39085 of 2008 before this Court, which asked the Licensing authority to decide the matter within three months.

legal_principles.principle: Something more than a temporary stay is required to give jurisdiction on the ground of 'residence'.
legal_principles.held: It must be more or less of a permanent character, and of such a nature that the court in which the respondent is sued, is his natural forum.
cited_cases: Smt. Jeewanti Pandey v. Kishan Chandra Pandey, (1982) AIR 3

legal_principles.principle: The word 'reside' is capable of being understood in its ordinary sense of having one's own dwelling permanently.
legal_principles.held: It means to make an abode for a considerable time: to dwell permanently or for a length of time; to have a seat.
cited_cases: Smt. Jeewanti Pandey v. Kishan Chandra Pandey, (1982) AIR 3

outcome.final_order: The order impugned has been set aside and the application for grant of firearm licence is allowed.
